# Ontology

<!-- Generated by `python -m chase.ontology.build`. Do not edit by hand. -->

What Talon Chase knows about, how those things relate, and the rules they obey.
The code is the source: `chase/domain/models.py` (entities and fields),
`chase/ontology/events.py` (evidence payloads), `chase/ontology/constraints.py`
(rules). This page and the two files under `ontology/` are generated from it,
and a test fails if they fall behind.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Version | `1.0.0` |
| Id | `urn:talonsight:talon-chase:ontology:1.0.0` |
| Schema SHA-256 | `ba6174884bdeae9ec203caf12255b48d4066fcbdfce0f450fc2689eb32db60ca` |
| Schema | [`ontology/talon-chase.schema.json`](../ontology/talon-chase.schema.json) |
| JSON-LD context | [`ontology/talon-chase.context.jsonld`](../ontology/talon-chase.context.jsonld) |

## Principles

* **Closed.** Every object lists all its fields; anything else is refused. Both
  stores validate every record they save and every event they append.
* **Typed references.** A field that holds an id names the entity it points at
  (`x-ref`). An empty optional reference means none.
* **Sensitive values are marked.** Fields marked sensitive (`x-sensitive`) hold
  what a carrier must never be told: rates, pickup numbers, customers,
  consignees. The outbound guard reads these marks; it has no list of its own.
* **History is not rewritten.** Consent is a sequence of records, not a flag.
  Evidence is a hash chain whose payloads have fixed shapes per kind.
* **Rules hold across records.** Each has a stable id, is checked after every
  test, and has a test that breaks it on purpose.
* **Versioned and hashed.** Exports carry the version and the schema's
  canonical SHA-256.

| Group | Purpose | Members |

| Need | What a load still needs, and the chase that obtains it. | [Requirement](#requirement), [Chase](#chase) |
| Exchange | Requests the agent decides on, their delivery, and what comes back. | [Attempt](#attempt), [OutboxMessage](#outboxmessage), [Inbound](#inbound) |
| Proof | Documents, the verdict on each, and the hash-chained record of everything. | [Document](#document), [Check](#check), [EvidenceEvent](#evidenceevent) |

## Who

The broker, its people, and the carriers and carrier contacts it works with.

### Broker

*entity*

A freight brokerage using Talon Chase.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Identifier. |
| `name` | string | Trading name, shown to carriers in every message. |
| `chase_mailbox` | string | The broker's own address that requests come from, e.g. pods@. |
| `rep_email` | string | Where packets and copied third requests go. |
| `sms_number` | string | The number texts come from; empty means no texts. |
| `adapter` | string | Where checked PODs are filed: an adapter name. |
| `outbound_enabled` | boolean | This broker's kill switch. |
| `config` | [BrokerConfig](#brokerconfig) | Schedule and policy. |

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `name` | string | Display name. |
| `role` | [OperatorRole](#operatorrole) | What they may do. |

## Proof

Documents, the verdict on each, and the hash-chained record of everything.

### Document

*entity*

A file received for a load.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Identifier. |
| `load_id` | string | The load it is filed under. → [Load](#load) |
| `inbound_id` | string | The message it came in. → [Inbound](#inbound) |
| `filename` | string | Name as sent. |
| `content_sha256` | string | SHA-256 of the bytes. |
| `received_at_ms` | integer | When it arrived. |
| `doc_type` | [DocType](#doctype) | What the reader says it is. |
| `extraction` | [Extraction](#extraction) | What the reader read from it. |

### Check

*entity*

The verdict on one document.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Identifier. |
| `chase_id` | string | The chase. → [Chase](#chase) |
| `document_id` | string | The document. → [Document](#document) |
| `result` | [CheckResult](#checkresult) | Pass, fail, exception or reroute. |
| `reasons` | list of string | Why, in short codes. |
| `checked_at_ms` | integer | When. |
| `reroute_load_id` | string | The load it belongs to instead, for REROUTE. → [Load](#load) (optional) |

### EvidenceEvent

*entity*

One entry in a load's hash chain. The payload's shape depends on the kind.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chain_id` | string | The load id, or broker:<id>, or system. |
| `seq` | integer | Position in the chain, from 0, no gaps. |
| `kind` | any | What happened. |
| `at_ms` | integer | When it happened. |
| `payload` | object | Details; see the payload definition for the kind. |
| `payload_digest` | string | SHA-256 of the canonical payload. |
| `prev_hash` | string | The previous event's hash; 64 zeros for the first. |
| `hash` | string | SHA-256 over the canonical header and prev_hash. |

## Outcome

Filing in the broker's system, and loads handed to a person.

### WriteBack

*entity*

One attempt to file a checked document in the broker's system.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Identifier. |
| `chase_id` | string | The chase. → [Chase](#chase) |
| `document_id` | string | The document being filed. → [Document](#document) |
| `adapter` | string | Which rung of the filing ladder. |
| `idempotency_key` | string | SHA-256 over (adapter, document hash, load). |
| `status` | [WriteBackStatus](#writebackstatus) | Pending, succeeded or failed. |
| `attempts` | integer | Adapter calls that returned an answer. |
| `receipt` | string | The adapter's receipt. |
| `detail` | string | Last error, or the pending reference. |
| `completed_at_ms` | integer or null | When it succeeded. |

### Escalation

*entity*

A load handed to a person, and how they finished it.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Identifier. |
| `chase_id` | string | The chase. → [Chase](#chase) |
| `load_id` | string | The load. → [Load](#load) |
| `broker_id` | string | The broker. → [Broker](#broker) |
| `reason` | [EscalationReason](#escalationreason) | Why a person is needed. |
| `detail` | string | What happened, in a sentence. |
| `created_at_ms` | integer | When. |
| `acknowledged_by` | string | The operator who finished it. → [Operator](#operator) (optional) |
| `acknowledged_at_ms` | integer or null | When they finished it. |
| `resolution` | [EscalationResolution](#escalationresolution) or null | How they finished it. |
| `note` | string | What they did, in their words. |

## Policy

How a broker wants chasing done, and who agreed to be texted.

### BrokerConfig

*value type*

Per-broker schedule and policy. Every value can be changed by the broker.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `no_status_grace_ms` | integer | Open a chase this long after the delivery appointment if the load has no status. |
| `sms_delay_ms` | integer | Text the driver this long after the first email. |
| `third_attempt_ms` | integer | Third request this long after the first. |
| `escalate_wait_ms` | integer | Hand to a person this long after the third request. |
| `min_gap_ms` | integer | Shortest gap between two requests. |
| `third_min_gap_ms` | integer | Shortest gap between the second and third requests. |
| `promise_grace_ms` | integer | How long a carrier's promise ('will send tomorrow') pushes the next ask back. |
| `reask_wait_ms` | integer | After a re-ask, wait this long before the plan continues. |
| `quiet_start_hour` | integer | Carrier-local hour when quiet hours begin. |
| `quiet_end_hour` | integer | Carrier-local hour when quiet hours end. |
| `morning_hour` | integer | Carrier-local hour of the second request. |
| `max_reasks` | integer | Re-asks for a failing document before a person decides. |
| `date_tolerance_ms` | integer | How far the POD's delivery date may be from the appointment. |
| `confidence_floor` | integer | Below this reading confidence (0 to 100), a person decides. |
| `writeback_retry_backoff_ms` | list of integer | Waits between filing retries; when it runs out, the next rung is tried. |
| `upload_link_ttl_ms` | integer | How long an upload link stays valid. |
| `send_retry_backoff_ms` | list of integer | Waits between delivery retries; when it runs out, the message fails. |

### Consent

*entity*

One recorded change to whether a contact may be texted. The record with the highest ``seq`` is the contact's current state.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Identifier. |
| `contact_id` | string | The contact this applies to. → [Contact](#contact) |
| `channel` | [Channel](#channel) | Always SMS for now. |
| `status` | [ConsentStatus](#consentstatus) | Granted or withdrawn. |
| `source` | [ConsentSource](#consentsource) | Where this record came from. |
| `recorded_at_ms` | integer | When it was recorded. |
| `seq` | integer | Position in this contact's consent history, from 1, in the order recorded. Decides which record is latest; times can tie and ids carry no order. |
| `recorded_by` | string | The operator who recorded it; empty when it came from the carrier or a sync. → [Operator](#operator) (optional) |
| `inbound_id` | string | The carrier message it came from, for a STOP reply. → [Inbound](#inbound) (optional) |
| `note` | string | Free text from the operator. |

## Value types

Stored inside an entity, never on their own.

### Attachment

A file referred to by its content hash.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `filename` | string | Name as sent. |
| `content_sha256` | string | SHA-256 of the bytes; the file is stored under it. |

### Plan

When each request in a chase is due, fixed when the chase opens.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `first_ms` | integer | First email. |
| `sms_ms` | integer | Driver text; 0 means none is planned. |
| `second_ms` | integer | Second request. |
| `third_ms` | integer | Third request. |
| `escalate_ms` | integer | Hand to a person if nothing has arrived. |

### Extraction

What the reader saw on a document.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `doc_type` | [DocType](#doctype) | What kind of document it is. |
| `readable` | boolean | Whether the page could be read at all. |
| `reference_numbers` | list of string | Load, BOL and PO numbers printed on it. |
| `signature_present` | boolean | Whether the receiver signed it. |
| `delivery_date_ms` | integer or null | Delivery date written on it. |
| `page_count` | integer | Pages received. |
| `exception_notes` | list of string | Shortage, damage or refusal noted by the receiver. |
| `confidence` | integer | How sure the reader is, 0 to 100. |

## Enumerations

### ChaseState

Where one chase for paperwork stands.

`OPEN`, `ASKED`, `RECEIVED`, `CHECKING`, `PASSED`, `FAILED_CHECK`, `FILED`, `CLOSED`, `ESCALATED`

### Step

The next thing a chase will do.

`FIRST_EMAIL`, `DRIVER_SMS`, `SECOND`, `THIRD`, `ESCALATE`, `REASK`, `WRITEBACK`, `NONE`

### Channel

How a message travels.

`EMAIL`, `SMS`, `UPLOAD`

### Role

A carrier contact's job.

`DISPATCHER`, `DRIVER`

### OperatorRole

What a person at the broker, or at TalonSight, may do.

`OWNER`, `STAFF`, `PLATFORM`

### PartyRole

A business on a load other than the broker and the carrier.

`CUSTOMER`, `SHIPPER`, `CONSIGNEE`

### DocType

What a document is.

`POD`, `LUMPER_RECEIPT`, `DETENTION_RECEIPT`, `SCALE_TICKET`, `CARRIER_INVOICE`, `RATE_CONFIRMATION`, `OTHER`

### RequirementStatus

Whether a load still needs a document.

`OPEN`, `MET`, `RESOLVED_BY_PERSON`

### CheckResult

`PASS`, `FAIL`, `EXCEPTION`, `REROUTE`

### EscalationReason

`NO_RESPONSE`, `RISK`, `UNKNOWN_SENDER`, `DOCUMENT_EXCEPTION`, `LOW_CONFIDENCE`, `NEEDS_HUMAN`, `WRONG_PERSON`, `WRITEBACK_FAILED`, `NO_CONTACT`, `REASK_LIMIT`, `OUTBOUND_BLOCKED`, `SEND_FAILED`

### EscalationResolution

How a person finished an escalation.

`HANDLED_BY_HAND`, `WAIVED`, `DISPUTED`, `OTHER`

### InboundStatus

`NEW`, `PROCESSED`, `HELD`, `UNMATCHED`

### OutboxStatus

`PENDING`, `SENDING`, `SENT`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`

### OutboxPurpose

`CARRIER_REQUEST`, `PACKET`

### WriteBackStatus

`PENDING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`

### ConsentStatus

`GRANTED`, `WITHDRAWN`

### ConsentSource

Where a consent record came from.

`RATE_CONFIRMATION`, `CARRIER_PACKET`, `WRITTEN`, `TMS_SYNC`, `STOP_REPLY`

| `writeback.failed` | `writeback_id`: str, `adapter`: str, `attempt`: int, `transient`: bool, `error`: str |
| `writeback.fallback` | `from`: str, `to`: str, `writeback_id`: str |
| `writeback.pending` | `writeback_id`: str, `adapter`: str, `reference`: str |
| `writeback.succeeded` | `writeback_id`: str, `adapter`: str, `receipt`: str, `idempotency_key`: str, `document_sha256`: str |

Retired kinds appear in older chains and verify as before; nothing records them
now and stores refuse to append them.

| Kind | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| `sms.stopped` | `contact_id`: str, `inbound_id`: str |

## Rules

Checked by `chase.ontology.constraints.check_store(store)`, which returns every
violation. The test suite runs all of them against every store it builds, and
the synthetic evaluation requires zero.

| Id | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| TC-01 | Every reference points at an existing entity of the named type. |
| TC-02 | Records only point at records of the same broker, in the right role. |
| TC-03 | A load has at most one chase, and a chase chases its own load's requirement. |
| TC-04 | A chase at rest is in a resting state whose next step fits it. |
| TC-05 | Request and re-ask counters stay within the schedule and the broker's limit. |
| TC-06 | A chase closed as filed has a passed document, a successful filing of it, a met requirement and a billable load. |
| TC-07 | A chase closed by a person has escalations, all resolved, and a requirement resolved by a person. No other closing reason exists. |
| TC-08 | An escalated chase has an open escalation; a chase still working has none. |
| TC-09 | An escalation is resolved all at once: by an operator, at a time, with a resolution; OTHER needs a note. |
| TC-10 | A requirement's status matches its evidence: MET names a passed document on the same load; closed requirements have a closing time; open ones have neither. |
| TC-11 | Every request is delivered by exactly one outbox message that matches it, and every carrier request in the outbox comes from a request. |
| TC-12 | An outbox message's fields match its delivery state. |
| TC-13 | A packet goes by email to the broker's own rep, with no quiet hours. |
| TC-14 | Every delivered text went to a contact who had consent at that moment. |
| TC-15 | A carrier message's status agrees with what was done with it. |
| TC-16 | Every file is stored under its hash, and every check judges a document of its own chase's load with reasons that fit the result. |
| TC-17 | A filing names a document of its chase's load, carries the agreed idempotency key, and a successful one has a receipt and a time. |
| TC-18 | Consent history is coherent: numbered 1, 2, 3... in the order recorded, with time never going backwards; STOP withdraws and names its message; written consent names an operator; after a STOP only written consent grants again. |
| TC-19 | Every evidence chain verifies, every load's chain starts with load.received, and every chase is on its load's chain. |
| TC-20 | No carrier request contains anything the ontology marks sensitive. |

## Changing the ontology

1. Change the models, payloads or rules.
2. Add an Alembic migration that carries existing data over and back.
3. Bump `ONTOLOGY_VERSION`: patch for wording, minor for something new and
   optional, major for anything an older reader would get wrong.
4. Run `python -m chase.ontology.build` and commit the result.
